questions.stem: Why is data described as a vital resource for a sole trader business?
options: data replaces the need for source documents and a general ledger
accurate data about sales, customers and costs supports better decisions
data is reported as a non-current asset in the Statement of Financial Position
collecting more data always increases the business's net profit
questions.explanation: Data such as sales by product, customer payment histories and costs lets the owner make informed decisions about pricing, inventory and credit. Data is not normally reported as an asset, and more data only helps if it is accurate and used well.

questions.stem: The owner of Jacaranda Gifts uses monthly sales data by product to set inventory reorder levels. This is an example of:
options: using data to inform practices of financial management
outsourcing an accounting process to an external provider
an external fraud control against payment redirection
capital expenditure on a non-current asset
questions.explanation: Analysing sales data to decide how much inventory to hold is using data to manage resources. Outsourcing involves an outside provider, and capital expenditure is spending on non-current assets.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts' customer list contains duplicate entries and out-of-date addresses. What is the main issue this creates?
options: the business's depreciation expense will be overstated for the year
decisions and communications based on the data will be unreliable
the business must report the list as a liability in its statements
the trial balance will no longer agree until the list is corrected
questions.explanation: Poor quality data leads to wasted marketing, missed customers and poor decisions, so data must be kept accurate and current. A customer list does not affect the trial balance or depreciation.

questions.stem: Cloud computing in accounting means:
options: keeping all accounting records on paper in a fireproof cabinet on the premises
installing accounting software on a single office computer that has no internet connection
sending source documents by post to an accountant at the end of each year
storing data and using software on a provider's servers, accessed over the internet
questions.explanation: Cloud accounting software and data are hosted by a provider and reached through the internet from any authorised device. Software installed on one office computer is a desktop system, not cloud computing.

questions.stem: Which is a benefit of cloud accounting software for a sole trader?
options: the owner and accountant can see up-to-date records from anywhere at the same time
the business no longer needs to keep any records for the Australian Taxation Office
the data can never be accessed by anyone other than the owner, whatever the controls
the software removes the need for any internal controls over cash and inventory
questions.explanation: Cloud systems give real-time, shared access, with updates and backups handled by the provider. Records must still be kept for tax purposes, and access depends on controls such as passwords, so security is not automatic.

questions.stem: Which is a risk of relying on cloud computing for business data?
options: the data can only be backed up once at the end of each year
an internet or provider outage can stop access to the records
the data must be printed out and re-entered by hand at the end of each month
the business cannot record any transactions involving GST
questions.explanation: Cloud systems depend on internet access and the provider's reliability and security, so outages or a breach at the provider affect the business. Cloud software handles GST, and providers usually back up data continuously.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts is moving its records to cloud accounting software. Which control would most reduce the risk of unauthorised access?
options: one shared password for all staff, written on the office whiteboard
leaving the software logged in on every computer to save time
giving every employee full access so no one is locked out
multi-factor authentication and a separate login for each user
questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication and individual logins make it much harder for outsiders to get in and let the owner see who did what. Shared passwords and open access remove accountability and make fraud easier.

questions.stem: Outsourcing accounting processes means:
options: training existing staff to perform every accounting task in the business
selling the business's accounts receivable to a bank for immediate cash
paying an external provider, such as a bookkeeper, to perform accounting tasks
moving the business's accounting records to a different office within the shop
questions.explanation: Outsourcing transfers tasks such as payroll, bookkeeping or BAS preparation to an outside specialist. Training staff keeps the work in-house.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of outsourcing payroll for a small sole trader?
options: the cost is always lower than doing the work in-house, whatever the size
access to specialist knowledge of pay rates and tax rules without hiring staff
the owner no longer has any legal responsibility for paying the staff correctly
the business's payroll data becomes impossible for outsiders to access
questions.explanation: An outsourced provider brings expertise and frees the owner's time. The business remains responsible for paying staff correctly, data still needs protecting, and outsourcing is not always cheaper.

questions.stem: Which is an issue with outsourcing accounting processes?
options: the owner has less direct control and must share confidential data with an outsider
the business is no longer able to prepare a Statement of Financial Position at year end
the business must stop using source documents for its transactions
the business can no longer claim GST credits on its purchases
questions.explanation: Outsourcing reduces the owner's direct control over timing and quality and exposes confidential data to a third party. Statements can still be prepared, and source documents and GST credits are unaffected.

questions.stem: The owner of Jacaranda Gifts outsources all bookkeeping and has not looked at a report for a year. What is the best recommendation?
options: outsource the remaining accounting tasks so the owner has nothing to review
stop keeping source documents, as the bookkeeper now holds the records
change bookkeepers every month so that no one becomes too familiar with the business
review monthly reports and bank statements, and keep direct access to the records
questions.explanation: Outsourcing does not remove the owner's need to monitor performance and detect errors or fraud. Regular review and direct access are key controls; constant changes of provider would add cost and confusion.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts sets its accounting software so that sales staff can enter invoices but cannot view or change payroll. Which control is this?
options: a backup control that protects the data against loss from a fire or a flood
an asset register control over the business's computers
access levels (user permissions) that limit each user to their own tasks
a physical control that keeps the computer in a locked room
questions.explanation: User permissions restrict each person to the data and functions they need, protecting confidential payroll data and supporting separation of duties. Physical and backup controls protect against other risks.

questions.stem: Why should a business keep regular backups of its accounting data in a separate location?
options: so that the business can report two sets of figures to the tax office
so that staff can change past transactions later without leaving any trace at all
so that the trial balance agrees even when transactions are missing
so records can be restored after a fire, hardware failure or ransomware attack
questions.explanation: Off-site or cloud backups allow the business to recover its records if the original data is lost, damaged or locked by criminals. Backups do not change the accuracy of the records themselves.

questions.stem: An employee receives an email that looks as if it is from the bank, asking them to log in through a link to 'confirm' account details. Which control best protects the business against this?
options: increasing the provision for doubtful debts at the end of the year
training staff to recognise phishing and to check requests through known contacts
giving the employee full administrator access to every part of the accounting software
storing all passwords in a shared spreadsheet so they can be recovered
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks people into handing over login details, so staff training and verifying requests by phoning a known number are key defences. Wider access and shared passwords make an attack more damaging.

questions.stem: Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an organisation covered by the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) whose data breach is likely to cause serious harm must:
options: record the breach as a bad debt in its accounts receivable ledger
notify the affected individuals and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
notify only its own staff and keep the breach confidential from customers and regulators
close the business until a court approves its new security controls
questions.explanation: The scheme requires covered organisations to tell affected people and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner about an eligible breach, so individuals can protect themselves. It does not require closing the business.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts keeps customers' names, addresses and card numbers in an unprotected spreadsheet on a laptop that staff take home. Which recommendation best addresses the risk?
options: print the spreadsheet and keep it on the front counter so staff can refer to it easily
keep the spreadsheet as it is but add more customers so it is more useful
stop storing card numbers, and encrypt and password-protect the remaining customer data
email the spreadsheet to every staff member so a copy is never lost
questions.explanation: Not keeping sensitive data that is not needed, and encrypting and restricting the rest, reduces both the chance and the harm of a breach. Sharing or printing the data widens the exposure.

questions.stem: Internal fraud is fraud committed by:
options: customers who do not pay their accounts by the due date
outsiders such as scammers who send fake invoices
suppliers who deliver goods later than they promised
people within the business, such as employees or managers
questions.explanation: Internal fraud is carried out by insiders, for example an employee who pays a fake supplier or pockets cash sales. Scammers outside the business commit external fraud, and late payment is not fraud.

questions.stem: Which is an example of external fraud against a business?
options: a cashier keeps the cash from some sales without ever recording them
a payroll clerk adds a fictitious employee to the weekly pay run
a manager claims private meals as business expenses
a scammer sends an invoice for advertising the business never ordered
questions.explanation: A fake invoice from an outsider is external fraud. The other options are carried out by people inside the business, so they are internal fraud.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts receives an email, apparently from a regular supplier, saying the supplier's bank account details have changed. What is the best control?
options: pay the supplier in cash from now on to avoid any bank account
phone the supplier on a number already on file to confirm before changing details
update the details in the system immediately so that the next payment is not made late
reply to the email asking the sender to confirm the new account
questions.explanation: Payment redirection scams rely on fake emails, so details must be verified independently through a known contact. Replying to the email only reaches the scammer.

questions.stem: A payroll clerk adds a fictitious 'ghost' employee and pays the wages into her own account. Which control would most directly prevent this?
options: the clerk takes the pay records home each night to keep them safe
the business pays all wages in cash rather than by bank transfer
the clerk is given access to change any record in the system
a different person approves new employees and reviews the pay run
questions.explanation: Separating the authorisation of new staff from processing pay, with independent review, means one person cannot create and pay a fake employee alone. More access and cash payments make the fraud easier.

questions.stem: Why do many businesses require staff in finance roles to take their annual leave and rotate duties?
options: it removes the need for separation of duties between staff
it means the business no longer needs to reconcile its bank account each month
someone else does the work while they are away, which can expose hidden fraud
it reduces the business's wages expense for the year by half
questions.explanation: Many frauds need constant concealment, so having another person perform the role can reveal irregularities. It complements, rather than replaces, separation of duties and reconciliations.

questions.stem: After an employee fraud is discovered, how is the business's accounting most likely affected?
options: the loss is added to the cost of non-current assets and depreciated
losses must be recognised and records corrected, and controls and reviews tightened
no change is needed, because fraud never affects the financial statements
the business must close all of its ledger accounts and open a completely new set of ledgers
questions.explanation: Fraud often overstates assets or expenses, so the loss must be recognised and the records corrected. The business should then review its practices of financial management, for example adding separation of duties or independent checks.

questions.stem: Capital expenditure is spending that:
options: pays for inventory that will be sold within the current period
pays the day-to-day wages and rent of the business
acquires or improves a non-current asset and benefits several future periods
keeps an existing asset in normal working order during the current period only
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure is recorded as an asset and allocated over future periods through depreciation. Routine maintenance, inventory and day-to-day expenses are other expenditure, recognised in the current period.

questions.stem: Which spending on a delivery van is capital expenditure?
options: the van's regular six-monthly service, oil change and new set of wiper blades
fuel used by the van on deliveries this month
replacing a cracked side mirror after a minor bump
replacing the engine, which extends the van's useful life by three years
questions.explanation: A new engine improves the asset and extends its useful life, so it is added to the asset's cost. Servicing, fuel and minor repairs keep the van running in the current period and are expenses.

questions.stem: Jacaranda Gifts records the $9,000 cost of new shop fittings as Repairs Expense. What is the effect on this year's and later years' profit?
options: this year's profit is overstated, and later years' profit is understated because depreciation is doubled
this year's and later years' profit are unaffected, because the cash paid is the same either way
this year's profit is understated, and later years' profit is also understated by depreciation
this year's profit is understated, and later years' profit is overstated because no depreciation is charged
questions.explanation: Expensing the full cost reduces this year's profit by $9,000 instead of one year's depreciation. In later years no depreciation is charged, so profit is overstated then. Cash is the same either way, but profit is spread incorrectly.

questions.stem: Which control applies to the purchase of non-current assets?
options: comparing quotes and requiring the owner's written authorisation before buying
letting any employee buy the equipment they want and claim the cost back later
recording the asset only when it is eventually sold
paying for equipment from the petty cash fund
questions.explanation: Authorisation and competitive quotes ensure assets are needed and bought at a fair price. Letting anyone buy assets without approval invites waste and fraud, and assets must be recorded when acquired.

questions.stem: Which control best protects the value of equipment during its use?
options: a maintenance schedule, with each service recorded in the asset register
waiting until equipment breaks down before any servicing is carried out
removing the equipment from the asset register once it is fully paid for
allowing staff to take equipment home without signing it out
questions.explanation: Planned maintenance extends useful life and reduces breakdowns, and recording it creates a history for each asset. Equipment should stay in the register while it is used, and movements should be authorised.

questions.stem: Which control applies to the sale of a non-current asset?
options: allowing the employee who uses it to sell it privately and keep the money from the sale
leaving the asset in the register so its cost is still shown
selling it without any record so the disposal does not affect profit
written authorisation, a fair sale price and removal from the asset register
questions.explanation: Disposals should be approved, sold at a fair value, recorded with any gain or loss, and removed from the register. Unrecorded or unauthorised sales hide theft and misstate the accounts.

questions.stem: In its annual check of the asset register against the shop floor, Jacaranda Gifts cannot find two laptops. What should happen?
options: increase the depreciation rate on all the other computers to make up the loss
investigate, record any loss if they are stolen or missing, and tighten controls
leave them in the register, as their cost was recorded correctly when bought
buy two identical laptops and add them to the register under the same identification numbers
questions.explanation: The register exists so physical checks can reveal missing assets. A loss should be investigated, written off if confirmed, possibly claimed on insurance, and controls such as tagging or sign-out improved.

questions.stem: Tagging each non-current asset with an identification number recorded in the asset register mainly helps to:
options: calculate the GST payable on the asset's purchase
increase the residual value of each asset
record each asset at its current market value
identify and locate each asset during physical checks
questions.explanation: Identification tags link each physical asset to its record, making stocktakes of assets and theft detection easier. They do not change GST, residual value or the historical cost basis.

questions.stem: Why is depreciation credited to Accumulated Depreciation rather than directly to the asset account?
options: so the asset's value is increased to its current market price each year
so that depreciation is treated as a liability owed to the asset supplier
so the asset can be removed from the register as soon as it is purchased
so the asset account keeps showing historical cost while the depreciation to date is shown separately
questions.explanation: Under the historical cost principle the asset account stays at cost, and Accumulated Depreciation, a negative asset account, records the cost allocated so far. Cost less accumulated depreciation gives the net value.

questions.stem: A shop fit-out costing $24,000 is bought on 1 January and depreciated at 30% a year on the diminishing balance method. The financial year ends on 30 June. What is depreciation for the first financial year?
questions.explanation: Part-year depreciation = 24,000 × 30% × 6/12 = $3,600. A full year gives $7,200. The following full year's depreciation would be (24,000 − 3,600) × 30% = $6,120.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet depreciation schedule, why are cost, residual value, useful life and rate placed in a separate input area?
options: so that the spreadsheet cannot calculate depreciation using formulae or functions
so the inputs are hidden from the owner and cannot be checked
so changing an input updates every formula and the report automatically
so the figures can be typed again in every row of the schedule
questions.explanation: Formulae that refer to input cells recalculate the schedule, net values and any graph when an input changes, supporting what-if analysis and reducing errors. Retyping figures in every row invites mistakes.
